events.description: A large ground-level explosion initiates at ~12.5s with a bright fireball, rapidly expanding into a rising fireball and then a mushrooming smoke plume that continues to grow and rise through 19.5s. Debris is visibly ejected upward and outward during the early phase (f1–f6), and the smoke column develops a classic cauliflower/mushroom shape by f7–f10, persisting with turbulent motion through f15.
A large ground-level explosion occurs, producing a rising plume of smoke and dust with a visible fireball at the base; the plume expands vertically and dissipates over time.

A large, rapidly expanding fireball erupts from ground level, followed by a rising column of smoke, debris, and water spray, characteristic of a high-energy explosion (likely involving fuel or volatile material). The event evolves from initial ignition (f1) through peak fireball (f2–f4), fragmentation and upward ejection (f5–f8), to a developing mushroom-like plume with mixed colors and sustained ejecta (f9–f15).
A large ground-level explosion occurs, producing a rapidly expanding fireball that transitions into a rising mushroom-shaped smoke plume over ~7.5 seconds.

A large, sustained explosion with a rising fireball and mushrooming smoke plume, followed by intense ground-level fire and debris ejection; consistent with a high-yield detonation in an open arid terrain.

A large, violent explosion occurs in a desert-like terrain, producing a rapidly expanding fireball and dense smoke plume; the blast appears to originate from ground level and propagates outward with significant force.

Secondary detonation or rapid combustion event visible as a bright flash and intensified fire within the ongoing smoke cloud, likely part of the same explosive sequence but distinct in timing and intensity.

A large, rapidly expanding fireball and smoke plume originating from ground level in a desert environment, evolving from an initial compact detonation into a massive, turbulent fireball with ejecta and rising mushroom-like cloud over ~7.5 seconds.
A large, sustained explosion with intense orange fireball and rapidly expanding dark smoke plume, evolving over ~7.5 seconds; initial fire diminishes as smoke dominates.

A large, sustained dust and smoke plume rises rapidly from the ground, expanding vertically and horizontally over time, consistent with a powerful explosion (e.g., large munition or IED detonation) in an arid environment. The plume shows turbulent billowing, mushroom-like development, and ground-level dust ejection throughout the sequence.

A large ground-level explosion in an arid, open landscape produces a rapidly expanding, bipartite (two-lobed) plume of gray smoke and dust that rises and billows over ~7.5 seconds. The initial blast is visible at f0 (187.0 s), with continued expansion and settling through f15 (194.5 s). A low dust wave propagates outward along the ground.
